_comment: Preguntas ORIGINALES tipo NIE del capítulo 3.3. No son preguntas reales del examen. Comprueba con tu edición 2027.

questions.scenario: Which is the correct definition of blackmail?
options: With a view to gain or intent to cause loss, making an unwarranted demand with menaces

questions.scenario: When is the offence of blackmail complete when the demand is sent by post?
A man writes to a businesswoman: 'Pay me £5,000 or I'll tell the press about your affair.' Is this 'menaces'?
options: No, menaces must be threats of violence
Yes – threats of any action detrimental or unpleasant can be menaces
Only if the affair is true
Only if she is a public figure

questions.scenario: What standard is used to judge whether a threat amounts to menaces (R v Clear)?
options: Whether the victim was actually scared
Whether a police officer would be scared
Whether the threat was in writing
Whether an ordinary person of normal stability and courage might be influenced to accede

questions.scenario: When is a demand with menaces 'warranted'?
options: When the maker believes he has reasonable grounds for the demand AND that the menaces are a proper means of reinforcing it

questions.scenario: A builder owed £2,000 texts the client: 'Pay by Friday or I'll break your legs.' Which is most likely?
options: Unwarranted – he can hardly believe that threatening violence is a proper means
Warranted, because the money is owed

questions.scenario: A man demands that a woman sleeps with him or he will post her intimate photos. Is this blackmail?
options: No – gain/loss must relate to money or other property; consider other offences

questions.scenario: Which of the following counts as 'gain' under s. 34?
options: Keeping what one has (money or property)

questions.scenario: A blackmail demand is made by text, but the victim ignores it and pays nothing. Is the offence complete?
options: Only if the victim is scared

questions.scenario: How is blackmail tried?
A man tells a shopkeeper: 'Give me £200 a week or your shop windows will get smashed.' Which offence is most accurate?
The nature of the act demanded in blackmail…
options: is immaterial (s. 21(2)), but there must be a view to gain or intent to cause loss in money/property

questions.scenario: Can a demand be implied rather than express?
options: Yes – a demand can be implied from words or conduct

questions.scenario: The defendant knows the victim is unusually timid and makes a threat that would not influence most people. Can this be menaces?
options: It may be – if he knows of the victim's timidity (⚠ R v Garwood)

questions.scenario: Whose belief matters for whether a demand is warranted?
explanations: The jury decides what he believed.

questions.scenario: Which is the maximum sentence for blackmail (⚠ check)?
A demand is made to cause loss to a business rival (to stop him bidding for a contract), with menaces. No gain for the defendant. Can this be blackmail?
options: Yes – intent to cause loss to another is enough

questions.scenario: Gain and loss include…
options: temporary or permanent gain/loss of money or property

questions.scenario: A man threatens to report his neighbour's genuine planning breach to the council unless she pays him £500. Which is correct?
options: Never blackmail because reporting is lawful
Can be blackmail – threatening a lawful act can still be menaces and the demand may be unwarranted
Only if the report is false

questions.scenario: Which pair is most accurate?
options: Blackmail = immediate force; robbery = future threats
Blackmail = menaces of anything detrimental, future OK; robbery = force then and there + theft
